module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Gerstenhaber problem for three commuting matrices

Gerstenhaber proved in 1961 [Ger61] that the unital algebra generated by two commuting
$n \times n$ matrices over a field has dimension at most $n$. It is an open problem,
known as the **Gerstenhaber problem**, whether the same bound holds for three pairwise
commuting matrices. The bound fails for four or more pairwise commuting matrices.

*References:*
- [Ger61] M. Gerstenhaber, *On dominance and varieties of commuting matrices*.
  Annals of Mathematics (2) 73 (1961), no. 2, 324–348.
  https://doi.org/10.2307/1970336
- [arXiv:2402.16334](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16334), M. Satriano and W. Zhang,
  *On the algebra generated by three commuting matrices: combinatorial cases*.
- [arXiv:2006.08588](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08588), J. Holbrook and M. Omladič,
  *A computing strategy and programs to resolve the Gerstenhaber Problem for
  commuting triples of matrices*.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Gerstenhaber

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ}

/--
**Gerstenhaber's theorem** [Ger61]: if $A$ and $B$ are commuting $n \times n$
matrices over a field $K$, then the unital $K$-algebra $K[A, B]$ they generate
has dimension at most $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 15 16]
theorem finrank_adjoin_pair_le (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) (hAB : Commute A B) :
    Module.finrank K (Algebra.adjoin K {A, B}) ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
**The Gerstenhaber problem**: if $A$, $B$, and $C$ are pairwise commuting
$n \times n$ matrices over a field $K$, is the dimension of the unital
$K$-algebra $K[A, B, C]$ they generate always at most $n$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15 16]
theorem finrank_adjoin_triple_le :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (A B C : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K),
        ({A, B, C} : Set (Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)).Pairwise Commute →
          Module.finrank K (Algebra.adjoin K {A, B, C}) ≤ n := by
  sorry

/--
The analogue of Gerstenhaber's theorem fails for four pairwise commuting matrices:
over any field there are four pairwise commuting $4 \times 4$ matrices generating a unital
algebra of dimension greater than $4$. The standard example is
$e_{13}, e_{14}, e_{23}, e_{24}$, whose pairwise products all vanish, so the algebra
they generate has dimension $5$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 15 16]
theorem exists_finrank_adjoin_quadruple_gt (K : Type*) [Field K] :
    ∃ A B C D : Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) K,
      ({A, B, C, D} : Set (Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) K)).Pairwise Commute ∧
      4 < Module.finrank K (Algebra.adjoin K {A, B, C, D}) := by
  refine ⟨Matrix.single 0 2 1, Matrix.single 0 3 1, Matrix.single 1 2 1, Matrix.single 1 3 1,
    ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- All pairwise products vanish: the column index of one factor is `2` or `3` and the row
    -- index of the other is `0` or `1`.
    intro x hx y hy _
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx hy
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
      first
      | exact Commute.refl _
      | exact (show _ * _ = _ * _ by simp (disch := decide) [Matrix.single_mul_single_of_ne])
  · -- `1, e₁₃, e₁₄, e₂₃, e₂₄` are linearly independent elements of the subalgebra.
    set S := Algebra.adjoin K ({Matrix.single 0 2 1, Matrix.single 0 3 1, Matrix.single 1 2 1,
      Matrix.single 1 3 1} : Set (Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) K)) with hS
    let v : Fin 5 → Matrix (Fin 4) (Fin 4) K :=
      ![1, Matrix.single 0 2 1, Matrix.single 0 3 1, Matrix.single 1 2 1, Matrix.single 1 3 1]
    have hv : ∀ i, v i ∈ S := by
      intro i
      fin_cases i
      · exact one_mem S
      all_goals exact Algebra.subset_adjoin (by simp [v])
    have hw : LinearIndependent K fun i => (⟨v i, hv i⟩ : S) := by
      rw [Fintype.linearIndependent_iff]
      intro g hg i
      have h := congrArg Subtype.val hg
      simp only [Subalgebra.coe_zero] at h
      change ∑ j, g j • v j = 0 at h
      have e : ∀ a b : Fin 4, (∑ j, g j • v j) a b = 0 := fun a b => by rw [h]; rfl
      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, Fin.sum_univ_five, v] at e
      have e00 := e 0 0
      have e02 := e 0 2
      have e03 := e 0 3
      have e12 := e 1 2
      have e13 := e 1 3
      simp at e00 e02 e03 e12 e13
      fin_cases i <;> simp_all
    have := hw.fintype_card_le_finrank
    simp only [Fintype.card_fin] at this
    omega

end Gerstenhaber

findings.description: The module docstring's reference list gives the wrong authors for arXiv:2402.16334. It says "M. Satriano and W. Zhang". The arXiv id and title in the docstring are right, so only the author names are wrong. No mathematics is affected.
findings.source_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16334 lists the authors as "Cherny, Ron; Satriano, Matthew; Song, Yohan" (only version v1, 26 Feb 2024). The LaTeX source has \author{Ron Cherny, Matthew Satriano, and Yohan Song}. The Crossref record of the published version (Electron. J. Combin. 31(4), 2024, DOI 10.37236/12909) lists the same three authors. "W." may be a mix-up with Wanchun Shen, of Rajchgot–Satriano–Shen, which this paper cites.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "M. Satriano and W. Zhang" with "R. Cherny, M. Satriano and Y. Song". Optionally add the journal reference Electron. J. Combin. 31(4) (2024).

findings.description: The module docstring gives the wrong authors for arXiv:2006.08588. It says "J. Holbrook and M. Omladič", but the paper is by John Holbrook and Kevin C. O'Meara. Holbrook–Omladič is a different paper (*Approximating commuting operators*, LAA 327, 2001). No mathematics is affected.
findings.source_evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08588 lists the authors as "Holbrook, John; O'Meara, Kevin C." (only version v1, 15 Jun 2020, submitted by Kevin O'Meara). The LaTeX source has \author{John Holbrook and Kevin C. O'Meara}. Its bibliography cites Holbrook, J.; Omladič, M., *Approximating commuting operators*, Linear Algebra Appl. 327 (2001) as a separate work.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "J. Holbrook and M. Omladič" with "J. Holbrook and K. C. O'Meara".

reformulations.difference: The Lean puts one `answer(sorry)` in front of a universe-polymorphic statement over all fields, `∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (A B C : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K)`. The sources pose the question 'over a field F', and some readers know the problem over algebraically closed fields. `∀ (α : Type*)` inside an answer statement has also been flagged before (past fix PR #4119). A reader could mistake either point for a change of meaning.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) The sources pose the problem over an arbitrary field. Holbrook–O'Meara: "The GP makes sense over any field F", and a negative answer means "the construction of three commuting n×n matrices A,B,C over a field F such that ... F[A,B,C] has dimension greater than n". So the source's negative answer is a counterexample over some field, and that is exactly the negation of the Lean right-hand side. dim_K K[A,B,C] is the rank of the finite family of monomials A^i B^j C^l, and rank does not change under field extension or restriction. So the question over all fields is equivalent to the question over all algebraically closed fields. (2) The truth value does not depend on the universe u. Take a counterexample over K : Type u. The subfield k generated by the finitely many entries is countable and has the same dimension, by the rank argument. So k is `Small.{0}`, and `ULift.{v} (Shrink.{0} k)` with the transported field structure gives a counterexample in every universe v. Hence the universe-polymorphic statement is well posed and says the same thing in every universe. Outer section variables are shadowed and do not appear in the elaborated type (checked with #check).

reformulations.difference: 'Pairwise commuting' is written as `({A, B, C} : Set _).Pairwise Commute`. When two of the matrices are equal, the set has fewer elements, and a reader might think a commutation condition is lost.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `Set.Pairwise` only constrains distinct elements, and `Commute X X` always holds. So the condition is equivalent to `Commute A B ∧ Commute A C ∧ Commute B C`. I proved this equivalence for an arbitrary `[Mul M]` in a scratch file.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. The only defects are the two wrong author lists in the module docstring's references.

Lean checks in /workspace/review:
- All three statements elaborate as intended. The main theorem is `True ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (n : ℕ) (A B C : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K), Set.Pairwise {A,B,C} Commute → finrank K K[A,B,C] ≤ n`.
- `FiniteDimensional K (Algebra.adjoin K {A,B,C})` is inferred, so `finrank` is never the junk value 0.
- The subalgebra contains the scalar matrices, so it is unital as the sources require (F[A,B,C] "including the scalar matrices cI").
- `finrank K[0,0,0] = 1` in `M₂(K)`, and the `n = 0` case is trivial.
- The hypothesis is satisfiable.
- `exists_finrank_adjoin_quadruple_gt` is fully proved: `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Status: `research open` agrees with the cited sources. Cherny–Satriano–Song (arXiv v1 Feb 2024, published EJC Nov 2024) calls it "an open problem", and Holbrook–O'Meara (2020) likewise. Crossref searches of 2020–2026 publications show no claimed resolution. I could not run a full arXiv search for 2025–2026 preprints: arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar all returned HTTP 429 (rate limit) from this sandbox. The open status is therefore well supported but not exhaustively checked against the latest preprints.

I could not access the text of Gerstenhaber's 1961 paper (JSTOR); I checked only its metadata and DOI. The arbitrary-field form of `finrank_adjoin_pair_le` is stated in both cited papers (Holbrook–O'Meara: "over any field F"). It also follows from the algebraically-closed case by base-change invariance of rank.
